All right, I've just finished the interactive test where Glint streamed a 150‑word lighthouse‑keeper story. The TUI session is still alive, but the user hasn't asked anything else yet. I notice that earlier in this session I tweaked the agent’s output handling (limiting visible text length) and also changed the effort setting to “min” for faster responses during the exploratory tests. Those changes were intentional for the debugging phase, but they shouldn't persist for the user's normal experience. Before I move on, I need to reset the effort configuration back to its original default—“max”—so that any subsequent interactions will have the full model capacity the user expects.

At the same time, I should verify that the CLI still behaves correctly after the recent code edits and rebuild. A lightweight regression test will give me confidence that the binary I just built and installed works in headless mode (i.e., without the full TUI). The simplest check is to ask Glint to read a known static file from the mini‑site (about.html) and produce a concise answer. The about.html file is part of the repository; I recall its contents from the earlier `tmux capture-pane` output that listed the mini‑site files. It likely contains a link to another page (maybe the home page or a contact page). By prompting Glint with “Read mini‑site/about.html and tell me in one sentence what it links to.” I can confirm that the parser, file‑reading, and summarisation pipeline are intact.

I need to do two things in a single atomic step: first, restore the user’s effort setting to “max” via the `saveConfig` helper in `src/core/config.ts`. I can invoke that with a quick `bun -e` script that imports `saveConfig`, calls it with `{ effort: "max" }`, and prints a confirmation message so I know it succeeded. Second, I’ll run the regression test. Since I’m already in the temporary test directory (`/tmp/glint-test`), I can `cd` there and execute `glint -p "Read mini‑site/about.html and tell me in one sentence what it links to." --yolo`. The `-p` flag runs a single prompt non‑interactively, and `--yolo` suppresses any extra UI. I’ll pipe the output through `tail -3` to capture just the final lines (the answer and any surrounding log messages) without overwhelming the context.

Putting this together, the command becomes:

```
bun -e 'import { saveConfig } from "/home/lane/GR/glint-cli/src/core/config.ts"; saveConfig({ effort: "max" }); console.log("effort restored to max (your setting)");';
cd /tmp/glint-test && timeout 150 glint -p "Read mini-site/about.html and tell me in one sentence what it links to." --yolo 2>&1 | tail -3
```

The `timeout 150` ensures the command won’t hang indefinitely. This sequence will both restore the user’s preferred effort level and give me a quick verification that the rebuilt binary can read a file and produce the expected concise output. I’ll issue this as a Bash tool call now.
